correctness.rationale: All-C6 strictly positive-curvature hypotheses justify uniform tangent graph expansions and chord inversion. The directional covariogram identity is exact; the fifth coefficient is (9 kappa^3+3 kappa_ss-5 kappa_s^2/kappa)/5760 per endpoint. The Gauss-map Jacobian and integration by parts give 9 kappa^4-8 kappa_s^2 after angular averaging. Radial integration gives the stated A, pi, 20160 normalization. The disk lens series, four independent ellipse integrals and sixteen harmonic tests agree; verify.py passes 33 checks. The explicit k=3,a=1/2 harmonic example has A=63 pi/64 and invariant -56 pi/(3 sqrt 3), proving strict sign change. Finite tests are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: The natural normalized two-point distance distribution motivates successive local geometric coefficients. The seventh coefficient is the first displayed order involving curvature variation, and its competition between fourth curvature power and squared curvature derivative permits negative values even though the preceding curvature-squared coefficient is positive. Exact one-threshold sign classification in each smooth harmonic family gives a meaningful qualitative geometric boundary and a shape descriptor that is not the known first-order perimeter term.
